summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with hematemesis, chest pain, and abdominal pain, in the context of chronic alcohol use and recent rectal bleeding. He presented intoxicated with a history of vomiting blood. Initial evaluation revealed severe anemia requiring transfusion. Endoscopy showed gastritis and grade I esophageal varices, with no active bleeding; the source was likely a Mallory-Weiss tear. Colonoscopy revealed angioectasias and grade 3 internal hemorrhoids, with one vessel clipped. Imaging confirmed cirrhosis and mild ascites. He developed dyspnea, with a chest X-ray showing early right lower lobe pneumonia, likely aspiration-related. He was treated with antibiotics, diuretics, and started on nadolol and lisinopril for portal hypertension and hypertension. Despite clinical improvement and a planned discharge with medication and follow-up instructions, the patient left against medical advice before completing the discharge process.
problems: Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, with bleeding
External hemorrhoids without mention of complication
Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
